```{r}
library(ggplot2)
```


# Part 1

```{r}
DF = read.table('data/bmd.csv', header = TRUE, sep = ',')
str(DF)
```
```{r}
colSums(is.na(DF))
```

```{r}
# sex, fracture, medication
unique(DF$sex)
DF$fsex = as.factor(DF$sex)

unique(DF$fracture)
DF$ffracture = as.factor(DF$fracture)

unique(DF$medication)
DF$fmedication = as.factor(DF$medication)

str(DF)
```
```{r}
DF$bmi = DF$weight_kg / (DF$height_cm / 100)^2
```

# Part 2

```{r}
summary(DF$bmi)
hist(DF$bmi)
```

```{r}
hist(DF$age) # Not normally distributed
boxplot(DF$age)
```

```{r}
ggplot(data = DF, aes(x = bmd, y = age)) +
    geom_point() # Very weak negative relationship
```

# Part 3

## How is BMD associated with age?

```{r}
fm1 = lm(bmd ~ age, data = DF)
coef(fm1)
```

> BMD = 1.046 - 0.004 * age

```{r}
anova(fm1)
```

age is significant in the model.

```{r}
coef(fm1)['(Intercept)']
```

The intercept (= 1.046) when age = 0 has no clinically meaningful interpretation.

```{r}
summary(fm1)
```

Stats:

- coefficient estimate of age = -0.004
- SE (age) = 0.000993
- t-value (age) = -4.162
- p-value (age) < 0.05 (significant)
- R^2 = 0.9399
- Adjusted R^2 = 0.08856
- Residual SE = 0.159 (167 df)

```{r}
confint(fm1, 'age', level = 0.95)
```

The 95% CI for age is the above range where it is the plausible range of values that the population regression coefficient of age.

# Part 4 - Assumptions for linear regression

```{r}
par(mfrow = c(2,2))
plot(fm1)
```

```{r}
plot(fm1, which = 4)
```

# Part 5 - Predicting

```{r}
# Age = 65
predict_x = data.frame(age = 65)
predict(fm1, predict_x)
predict(fm1, predict_x, interval = 'confidence', level = 0.95)
predict(fm1, predict_x, interval = 'prediction', level = 0.95)
```
